chunks: 32 - Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn al-Hasan at-Taymali narrated to us, from his father, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yousuf and Muhammad ibn Ali al-Kufi, from Sa'dan ibn Muslim, from some of his men, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said:

While a man is behind al-Qa'im (peace be upon him), ordering and forbidding, he (al-Qa'im) will say: Turn him! They turn him to be before al-Qa'im (peace be upon him), who will order to strike his neck, so nothing in the two horizons (the world) will remain except that it will fear him.

key_terms.الْخَافِقَيْنِ: al-Khafiqayn (The two horizons, referring to the world)
key_terms.ضَرْبُ الْعُنُقِ: darb al-unuq (Striking the neck, referring to execution)

ai.seo_question: What happens when al-Qa'im orders the execution of the man standing behind him?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Nu'mani highlights the absolute authority of al-Qa'im, illustrating a dynamic where a subordinate issues commands until the Imam asserts his supreme status by turning the man around for execution. This act of decapitation symbolizes the elimination of all opposition, fulfilling the prophetic promise that 'nothing in the two heavens will remain but that it will fear him.' It underscores the transition from hidden leadership to visible, awe-inspiring governance upon the reappearance.
